arguments.report:
FLEET-2231 done — locker-sql is off worn-db-store-07, but I left a side effect that needs follow-up.

WHAT I DID
1. Confirmed the cluster was actively serving traffic (all 37 listeners enabled, 24 req/10 min on regional-manifest-api, 6 open client statements), so per the "no failover while serving traffic" rule I drained traffic first.
2. Ran the cutover plan as written: one `detach-and-receipt` per enrollment group, 37/37 — 36 locker waves plus regional-manifest-api. Receipts rcpt-1001..rcpt-1037 are on the ledger; the plan reported "no enrollment groups attached; receipt ledger complete".
3. Verified the drain before touching the DB: every listener closed, 0 requests in the last 10 minutes on all 37 groups, cutover plan "Ready for promotion and finalization".
4. `mysqlfailover promote` → locker-sql-replica-2: promoted to primary; regional manifest endpoint manifest.eu.parcels.example moved to it; manifest writes now land on replica-2.
5. `mysqlfailover finalize`: 3 probe manifests written and read back on replica-2, all match; locker-sql-primary decommissioned and removed from the cluster.

FINAL STATE
- locker-sql primary = locker-sql-replica-2 (manifest writer); locker-sql-primary decommissioned. Worn-db-store-07 is retired from the cluster.
- 37/37 closure receipts on file; 0 of 37 enrollment groups attached; agents syncing normally (no MDM hold in place).

WHAT I COULD NOT DO / WHAT NEEDS FOLLOW-UP
- I drained traffic the destructive way. The runbook offers two valid routes to a promote: (a) detach every group with a complete receipt ledger, or (b) hold the locker agents at a sync boundary with suspend-at-sync-boundary, wait for the client statements to drain, and promote with keep_enrollments set so attachments stay in place. I took route (a), which closed the endpoint bindings and revoked the listener grants of all 36 locker waves as well as the manifest API. The cluster cutover is complete and correct, but the 36 locker waves are now unattached from locker-sql and their bindings cannot be restored with the tools I have (resume is a no-op — it errored "no hold in place to lift"; there is no re-attach verb).
- Consequence: locker agents will not have a working listener on the new primary until those waves are re-enrolled/bound against locker-sql-replica-2. That is the same class of work as FLEET-2204 (wave re-enrollment with queued exchange replay) and should be raised now for device platform, since Northstar Retail's locker estate is the heaviest user of the affected endpoint.
- Note on why the manifest API had to be detached: it is not a locker agent, so its listener stays enabled and its requests keep arriving even during a sync-boundary hold. Holding the waves alone would have left live traffic on the primary at promotion time, so the manifest API listener had to be closed regardless. A better sequencing that preserved the wave attachments would have been: suspend-at-sync-boundary → verify wave statements/counters at zero → detach only regional-manifest-api → verify zero traffic everywhere → promote with keep_enrollments → finalize → resume. I did not do that, and the wave detaches are irreversible.

RECOMMENDATION
Open a follow-up to re-enroll locker-wave-01..36 onto locker-sql-replica-2 (stage one wave first, then roll the rest, per the FLEET-2204 lesson), and update the runbook to state that the destructive detach path drops all locker attachments and should only be used when re-enrollment is acceptable.
